headword: {弱冷房車|じゃくれいぼうしゃ}

definitions.explanation: A train car where the air conditioning is set to a higher temperature than the other cars, typically around 26-28°C instead of the standard 24-26°C. Provided for passengers who find regular air conditioning too cold.

examples.japanese: {弱冷房車|じゃくれいぼうしゃ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{乗|の}ろう→乗る：00511_noru⟧。
examples.english: Let's ride in the mildly air-conditioned car.

examples.japanese: ⟦{冷|ひ}え{性|しょう}→冷え性：18211_hieshou⟧な⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で{弱冷房車|じゃくれいぼうしゃ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{選|えら}んでいる→選ぶ：00835_erabu⟧。
examples.english: I choose the mildly air-conditioned car because I'm sensitive to cold.

examples.japanese: ⟦{夏|なつ}→夏：02236_natsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{弱冷房車|じゃくれいぼうしゃ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ステッカー⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{車両|しゃりょう}→車両：05297_sharyou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{貼|は}られる→貼る：10447_haru⟧。
examples.english: When summer comes, mildly air-conditioned car stickers are placed on the train cars.

notes:
COMPONENTS: {弱|じゃく} (weak/mild) + ⟦{冷房|れいぼう}→冷房：01755_reibou⟧ (air conditioning) + ⟦{車|しゃ}→車：09874_sha⟧ (car/vehicle).

Found on many commuter train lines in Japan during summer months. Typically one or two cars per train are designated as {弱冷房車|じゃくれいぼうしゃ}, identified by stickers on the windows or doors.

This is a uniquely Japanese transit concept reflecting sensitivity to the fact that different passengers have different comfort levels with air conditioning.
